entry.title: KLPR2022 Lemma 1, Eq. (1) (main text p.5; proof SI Note IV)
entry.subtitle: s_money_kent_2022_ideal_2site · A. Kent, D. Lowndes, D. Pitalua-Garcia, J. Rarity. Practical quantum tokens without quantum memories and experimental tests. npj Quantum Information 8, 28 (2022). doi:10.1038/s41534-022-00524-4

fields.label: Source and theorem
fields.text: KLPR2022 Lemma 1, Eq. (1) (main text p.5; proof SI Note IV): IQT1 and IQT2 are eps_unf-unforgeable with eps_unf = (1/2 + 1/(2*sqrt(2)))^N.

fields.label: Assumptions
items: Ideal schemes IQT1/IQT2 of Table 1: N exact BB84 qubits with uniformly random states and bases; no loss, no preparation/measurement error, no multiphoton component.
Bob (the bank) follows the scheme honestly; Bob's agents communicate over secure authenticated channels; Alice is arbitrary (unforgeability quantifies over dishonest Alice).

fields.label: Finite n or asymptotic
fields.text: exact upper bound for every finite N >= 1

fields.label: Parameters
fields.text:
N: number of transmitted qubits, integer >= 1
M: presentation-point pairs; the ideal bound is stated for M = 1 only (optional, default 1)

fields.label: Quantifier over adversaries
fields.text: for every (unbounded quantum) strategy of dishonest Alice, P[Bob accepts at both presentation points] <= eps_unf

fields.label: Caveats
items: Not Wiesner's 3/4 bound. Not valid for the realistic schemes QT1/QT2 (use P-S2). No multi-site (M>1) version is stated for the IDEAL schemes; Theorem 2 concerns QT^M only.
Privacy of IQT is argued in prose only (main text p.4); no numbered privacy lemma for IQT, so the evaluator returns no privacy value for S1.
